structured.approach: I followed DE-02 in the data-engineering-steps skill. First I read feat.tasks to find this lane's tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. The permission table is restricted, so I read it through the tool view, which says no secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline. The hook blocks shell commands in this step, so I checked the code with Grep and Read instead. I searched the whole checkout for environment-variable, credential, Databricks and network patterns and found none. I also read pipeline.py, ingest.py, transform.py, dq.py, schedule.json and ci.py. Two approved background items backed this up: task.repo_access (no Databricks or workspace) and the design's SE-4 / CL-X9 entries (no secrets added; synthetic data only). Then I wrote task.secrets_scope with names only. Its result is that no secret is required or granted and no access request is needed. One open question is non-blocking: whether the DE-13 scheduler will need a credential.

claims.text: The Data Engineering lane tasks are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in ap_pipeline.
The permission table states that no secrets are required or granted for the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-02's delays_by_vendor is a pure function with no I/O, and TSK-01 changes only transform.py, __init__.py and tests/test_pipeline.py; neither touches ingest.py, pipeline.py or schedule.json.
The pipeline takes the feed as text: run(csv_text) calls parse_feed, then to_model, then quality_report. It opens no connection to a source system.
A search of the ap_pipeline checkout for environment-variable, secret, credential, Databricks and network patterns found no match, and ci.py reads no environment variable or credential.
The design adds no secrets or personal data (SE-4), and test data is synthetic only (CL-X9).
Databricks or another workspace is not used by this lane, so no workspace credential is needed.
schedule.json sets frequency daily at 02:00 in Asia/Kolkata; no input names the scheduler platform or its credential needs.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): DE-13 will schedule the pipeline (schedule.json: daily, 02:00, Asia/Kolkata), but no input names the scheduler platform or says whether it needs a credential. Interim: no secret now; re-run DE-02 if DE-13 names a scheduler that needs one. Owner: Data engineering lead.
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope for FEAT-ZD-48600. The lane's tasks, TSK-01 and TSK-02 in ap_pipeline, need no secrets, and the permission table grants none for the repository. So the granted secret names are "none" and no access request was raised. The code check backs this up: the code reads no environment variables, credentials or network sources. The design adds no secrets either (SE-4). There are no blocking questions. One non-blocking question asks whether the scheduler at DE-13 will need a credential.

tool_input.command: git ls-files && grep -rniE "environ|getenv|secret|token|password|api_key|credential|dbutils|databricks" --include=* . | grep -v "^./.git/" | head -30; cat src/ap_pipeline/schedule.json 2>/dev/null || find . -name schedule.json -not -path './.git/*' -exec cat {} \;
tool_input.description: List repo files and search for secret usage
